item.title: Mbappe double helps Real Madrid sweep aside Sevilla ahead of El Clasico
item.description: Kylian Mbappe scored twice as Real Madrid closed the gap on LaLiga leaders Barcelona to six points with a 4-1 win over Sevilla at the Santiago Bernabeu on Sunday, a week before the rivals meet.
item.dc:creator: Ruairidh Barlow
item.content:encoded: Kylian Mbappe scored twice as Real Madrid closed the gap on LaLiga leaders Barcelona to six points with a 4-1 win over Sevilla at the Santiago Bernabeu on Sunday, a week before the rivals meet. Arda Guler opened the scoring in the 30th minute, arrowing a shot into the top corner from outside the box, before Mbappe added a second seven minutes later after a brilliant turn. Mbappe won and converted a penalty in the 63rd minute to effectively settle the contest. Sevilla pulled one back with 10 minutes remaining through substitute Manu Bueno, but Yan Diomande restored Real's three-goal lead with a thunderous strike two minutes later. Real climbed to third on 21 points, one behind Atletico Madrid, while Sevilla are sixth on 14.

item.title: Aaron Rodgers delivers another comeback as Steelers beat Bucs in OT
item.description: Aaron Rodgers threw touchdown passes in the fourth quarter and overtime and Chris Boswell made four field goals to lead the Pittsburgh Steelers to a 26-19 comeback win in overtime over the host Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Aaron Rodgers threw touchdown passes in the fourth quarter and overtime and Chris Boswell made four field goals to lead the Pittsburgh Steelers to a 26-19 comeback win in overtime over the host Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday. The Steelers (4-2) erased a 16-3 fourth quarter deficit with 16 unanswered points in the period. The Bucs (1-5) tied the game at 19 with three seconds left on a 53-yard field goal by Chase McLaughlin. In overtime, Rodgers led a 12-play, 70-yard drive, capped by a 6-yard touchdown pass to Germie Bernard with 3:15 left in overtime. Bernard caught 11 passes for 87 yards and DK Metcalf caught 11 passes for 93 yards. Jalon Daniels, who made his third consecutive start for injured Baker Mayfield (thumb), scrambled 10 yards to Tampa Bay's own 37 for a first down on fourth-and-nine on the Bucs' ensuing drive. Five plays later, Daniels was sacked on fourth down by Jalen Ramsey on a corner blitz to end the game. According to Pro Football Reference, it was Rodgers' 27th career fourth-quarter comeback. Rodgers completed 33 of 49 passes for 253 yards, two touchdowns and one interception. Pittsburgh's defense sacked Daniels five times and intercepted him twice. Daniels completed 22 of 43 for 164 and a touchdown. Jamel Dean picked off Daniels and returned it 40 yards to the Bucs' 3 with 1:38 to go in the fourth. Tampa Bay kept Pittsburgh out of the end zone on three consecutive plays, but the Steelers took a 19-16 on Boswell's fourth field goal - a 20-yarder with 1:21 left. After coming up with only a Boswell 52-yard field goal on their first 10 possessions, the Steelers finally found the end zone with 13:48 left in the fourth. Rodgers connected with Darnell Washington on a 5-yard touchdown to cut Pittsburgh's deficit to 16-10. Pittsburgh regained possession when rookie Daylen Everette intercepted Daniels at the Bucs' 45. But after Rodgers was sacked for the fourth time, Pittsburgh settled for another Boswell field goal, cutting the lead to 16-13 with 8:08 left. Tampa Bay led 13-0 until just before halftime thanks to two McLaughlin field goals and Daniels' lone touchdown pass from 2 yards out to Emeka Egbuka with 14:52 left in the second quarter. --Field Level Media

item.title: Danish duo fire high-flying Lazio to 3-0 win over Juventus
item.description: Lazio's Danish duo made the difference in Turin as Oliver Provstgaard and Gustav Isaksen scored in a 3-0 win over Juventus on Sunday that lifted their side level with Inter Milan at the top of Serie A.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Lazio's Danish duo made the difference in Turin as Oliver Provstgaard and Gustav Isaksen scored in a 3-0 win over Juventus on Sunday that lifted their side level with Inter Milan at the top of Serie A. Provstgaard broke the deadlock in the 37th minute, using his height to glance home Mattia Zaccagni's cross after Lazio worked a short corner on the left. Fellow Dane Isaksen doubled the lead in the 66th minute, collecting a pass from Tavares on the right before shifting the ball onto his left foot and bending a low finish into the far corner. Fisayo Dele-Bashiru completed the scoring in the 89th minute, launching a counter-attack from inside his own half and driving into the box before slotting home a low finish as frustrated home supporters jeered Juventus through to the final whistle. Lazio have 19 points from seven matches, level with Inter, who maintained their unbeaten start to the domestic season with a 3-1 [USN:L6N46307R TEXT:"comeback "]victory over Bologna on Saturday. MILAN SURVIVE ATALANTA FIGHTBACK AC Milan survived a late Atalanta fightback to claim an entertaining 3-2 home victory earlier on Sunday. The hosts opened the scoring in the 24th minute through a Goncalo Ramos penalty, before Adrien Rabiot doubled their advantage shortly before the break. Mario Gila made it 3-0 in the 57th minute, seemingly putting the contest beyond Atalanta. However, Gianluca Gaetano reduced the deficit in the 66th minute and Nikola Krstovic added a second for Atalanta in the 81st to set up a tense finish. Two minutes later, Mike Maignan rushed out to deny Davide Zappacosta in a one-on-one, parrying the effort with his legs to preserve Milan's lead. Fiorentina's struggles continued as they suffered a 3-1 defeat at home to Como, leaving them second from bottom in the table with four points from seven matches. Quickfire goals from Mattia Liberali and Nico Paz around the half-hour mark put Como in command before Marin Pongracic pulled one back before the break, but Anastasios Douvikas sealed the victory for the visitors early in the second half. Como are fifth with 14 points.

item.title: Bryce Young, Panthers control banged-up Eagles
item.description: Bryce Young threw two touchdown passes to Tommy Tremble and the Carolina Panthers were solid defensively in a 25-14 road victory against the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday afternoon.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Bryce Young threw two touchdown passes to Tommy Tremble and the Carolina Panthers were solid defensively in a 25-14 road victory against the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday afternoon. Chuba Hubbard rushed for 120 yards and one touchdown on 28 carries. Young finished 20-for-39 for 281 yards. Ryan Fitzgerald kicked two long field goals to help the Panthers (3-2) to their second road triumph in three trips this year. Quarterback Tanner McKee threw for 215 yards and one touchdown in his season debut, but the Eagles (2-4) lost their fourth consecutive game. McKee, appearing in his seventh career game, filled in because quarterback Jalen Hurts was out after he was diagnosed with a concerning blood clot in his leg during the past week. The Eagles punted eight times and collected 17 first downs. Fitzgerald's 52-yard field goal on the first possession of the second half marked the only scoring in the third quarter. The Panthers went on a 92-yard drive that concluded with Hubbard's 1-yard TD run early in the fourth quarter. A two-point conversion pass failed, leaving the score at 19-7. The Eagles bounced back on McKee's 19-yard touchdown throw to DeVonta Smith with 10:42 to play. After a blocked Eagles punt gave Carolina favorable field position, the Panthers needed to go only 48 yards for an insurance touchdown, with Young connecting with Tremble on a 19-yard touchdown play with 6:34 left. Carolina went up 10-0 on Young's 12-yard pass to Tremble in the second quarter. Dameon Pierce put the Eagles on the board with a 2-yard run with 2:42 remaining in the first half. Carolina outgained the Eagles 178-110 in the first half, which ended at 10-7. The Panthers, fresh off an open week on the schedule, produced Fitzgerald's 47-yard field goal on their first possession. Philadelphia's first two possessions resulted in a net of minus-3 yards. The Eagles punted three times in the first quarter. --Field Level Media

item.title: Saints build big lead, then need to hold off Giants for win
item.description: Tyler Shough threw three touchdown passes and ran for a touchdown and the visiting New Orleans Saints held off the New York Giants 34-27 on Sunday afternoon in East Rutherford, N.J.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Tyler Shough threw three touchdown passes and ran for a touchdown and the visiting New Orleans Saints held off the New York Giants 34-27 on Sunday afternoon in East Rutherford, N.J. The Saints (2-4) ended a three-game losing streak as they rushed for a season-high 175 yards and Martin Emerson Jr. had two of the team's three interceptions. Jameis Winston passed for one touchdown and two interceptions for the Giants (3-2-1) before being replaced by J.J. McCarthy, who led a dramatic late comeback. On the first possession of the second half, Shough threw a short pass to Alvin Kamara, who turned the play into a 31-yard touchdown that gave New Orleans a 17-10 lead. Shough sneaked 1 yard for a touchdown and the Saints' fourth score in as many possessions, pushing the lead to 24-10. Daniel Carlson's 51-yard field goal increased the lead to 27-10 at the end of the third quarter. Julian Blackmon's interception of Winston led to Shough's 18-yard touchdown pass to Chris Olave to expand the lead to 34-10. McCarthy replaced Winston and threw an interception before driving the Giants to Tyrone Tracy Jr.'s 5-yard touchdown and a subsequent 2-point conversion, McCarthy's 24-yard touchdown pass to Isaiah Likely (with a failed 2-point try) and Dominic Zvada's 41-yard field goal to trim the lead to 34-27 with 2:04 left. New York forced a punt and McCarthy, who finished with 243 passing yards, drove the Giants to the Saints 14, but they turned the ball over on downs with five seconds left. Malik Nabers finished with 12 catches for 165 yards for New York. The Giants' second possession was a 12-play, 93-yard drive that ended with Winston's 17-yard touchdown pass to Tracy to give them a 7-0 lead at the end of the first quarter. Zvada's 34-yard field goal increased the lead to 10-0. Carlson kicked a 58-yard field goal for New Orleans' first points, and on the ensuing kickoff Charlie Jones fumbled and Oscar Delp recovered for the Saints at the New York 28. On fourth-and-goal, Shough threw a 2-yard touchdown pass to Bryce Lance to tie the score 10-10 at halftime. --Field Level Media

item.title: McLaren venderá cinco monoplazas de F1, todos ellos pilotados por campeones y uno por Brad Pitt
item.description: McLaren va a poner a la venta cinco monoplazas de Fórmula 1 en perfecto estado de funcionamiento pilotados por campeones, entre ellos Lewis Hamilton y el difunto brasileño Ayrton Senna, y uno de los cuales también fue probado por el actor de Hollywood Brad Pitt.
item.dc:creator: Alan Baldwin
item.content:encoded: McLaren va a poner a la venta cinco monoplazas de Fórmula 1 en perfecto estado de funcionamiento pilotados por campeones, entre ellos Lewis Hamilton y el difunto brasileño Ayrton Senna, y uno de los cuales también fue probado por el actor de Hollywood Brad Pitt. Los monoplazas, que se venderán a través del concesionario de lujo Tom Hartley Jr. y de los que se espera que recauden decenas de millones de dólares, serán puestos a punto por los actuales campeones de constructores para sus próximos propietarios. Hartley Jr. también vendió la colección del antiguo magnate de la F1 Bernie Ecclestone y 20 coches de carretera que pertenecían al fallecido copropietario de McLaren, Mansour Ojjeh. "Hemos decidido desprendernos de estos emblemáticos coches de Fórmula 1 de McLaren porque creemos que tenerlos simplemente guardados en un almacén es un flaco favor a lo que representan», declaró el domingo Zak Brown, director ejecutivo de McLaren Racing, en un comunicado. "Estos coches se fabricaron para ser conducidos y competir, y queremos que se utilicen y se disfruten. Creemos que esa es la mejor manera de mantener viva nuestra historia y activa nuestra actividad relacionada con el patrimonio".

item.title: La policía de Milán se enfrenta a los manifestantes en el segundo día de disturbios
item.description: La policía de Milán se enfrentó el domingo a manifestantes que lanzaban piedras y saqueaban tiendas durante las protestas contra la mala calidad de los servicios y el aumento del costo de la vida, un día después de que se produjeran disturbios similares en varias ciudades italianas.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: La policía de Milán se enfrentó el domingo a manifestantes que lanzaban piedras y saqueaban tiendas durante las protestas contra la mala calidad de los servicios y el aumento del costo de la vida, un día después de que se produjeran disturbios similares en varias ciudades italianas. La policía antidisturbios lanzó gases lacrimógenos y utilizó cañones de agua después de que varios cientos de manifestantes encapuchados rompieran escaparates y prendieran fuego a papeleras en la zona cercana a la céntrica Piazza Duomo, según informaron a Reuters fuentes conocedoras de la investigación. Más de 60 manifestantes fueron trasladados a la comisaría para ser sometidos a controles adicionales, añadieron las fuentes. Un total de 28 manifestantes fueron detenidos tras los enfrentamientos similares que estallaron el sábado en ciudades del norte, entre ellas Milán, Bolonia, Brescia, Bérgamo y Turín, según un reporte policial del domingo. Los enfrentamientos recordaron la violencia vivida en la vecina Francia, donde cientos de miles de personas, indignadas por el aumento de los precios y el deterioro de los servicios públicos, salieron a las calles el sábado en algunas de las protestas más violentas que se han vivido en el país en los últimos años. La primera ministra italiana, Giorgia Meloni, que se enfrenta a unas elecciones el año que viene, condenó la violencia y anunció una reunión del Gobierno el lunes para debatir cómo abordar la situación.

item.title: Anthropic destinará una participación del 5 % a un nuevo fondo de interés público
item.description: Anthropic anunció el domingo que destinará el 5 % de sus acciones a un nuevo fondo de interés público, siempre que los accionistas lo aprueben, y que dicha participación podría aumentar a medida que crezca la valoración del gigante de la inteligencia artificial.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Anthropic anunció el domingo que destinará el 5 % de sus acciones a un nuevo fondo de interés público, siempre que los accionistas lo aprueben, y que dicha participación podría aumentar a medida que crezca la valoración del gigante de la inteligencia artificial. El fondo propuesto se constituiría como una sociedad de responsabilidad limitada de propiedad exclusiva y recibiría un 2 % adicional de las acciones de Anthropic, a discreción del consejo de administración, por cada aumento del 50 % en el valor de la empresa por encima de un umbral de referencia que aún no se ha revelado. El Fondo de Beneficio Público de Anthropic podría apoyar iniciativas como donaciones a organizaciones sin ánimo de lucro, distribuciones directas a poblaciones específicas e iniciativas para abordar el impacto de la IA en los trabajadores. La empresa ha afirmado que ninguna parte del capital social del fondo se utilizaría para actividades de cabildeo ni para contribuciones políticas, ni en Estados Unidos ni en el extranjero. El creador del asistente de IA Claude tiene previsto llevar a cabo una de las mayores salidas a bolsa de la historia como sociedad de beneficio público, una estructura jurídica que exige a la dirección tener en cuenta determinados intereses más amplios, además de generar beneficios para los inversores. La empresa, que se ha posicionado como una entidad que antepone la seguridad, ha destacado a menudo los riesgos asociados a sus modelos de IA, más recientemente en el folleto de su salida a bolsa, en el que se indicaba que estos podrían mostrar "comportamientos de autoconservación", según informó Reuters en exclusiva en septiembre. Si se suma el nuevo fondo, aproximadamente el 20 % de las acciones de Anthropic se destinaría a fines públicos, sin contar las acciones adicionales que podrían asignarse si la empresa alcanza futuros hitos de valoración. Anthropic ha afirmado que revelará más detalles en los próximos meses sobre la gobernanza del fondo, su estructura y los umbrales de valoración que podrían ampliar su participación accionarial. También tiene previsto publicar un informe de beneficio público en el que se detallen los avances hacia el cumplimiento de su misión.

item.title: Caleb Williams shines in return as Bears knock off Falcons
item.description: ATLANTA - Caleb Williams returned from a three-game absence to complete 30 of 36 passes for 305 yards and a touchdown to help the visiting Chicago Bears stave off the Atlanta Falcons for a 31-23 victory on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: ATLANTA - Caleb Williams returned from a three-game absence to complete 30 of 36 passes for 305 yards and a touchdown to help the visiting Chicago Bears stave off the Atlanta Falcons for a 31-23 victory on Sunday. Williams showed little rust after suffering a hamstring tear on Sept. 20, connecting with eight different receivers for the Bears (4-2), who won their third game in four tries. D'Andre Swift rushed for two touchdowns for Chicago, which saw its 24-point fourth-quarter lead dwindle to eight before holding on. Michael Penix Jr. completed 19 of 33 passes for 225 yards and three touchdowns for Atlanta (2-4), which dropped its second straight. After building a 14-point halftime advantage, Chicago tacked on with Roschon Johnson's 4-yard touchdown run to extend the lead to 28-7 with 1:48 left in the third quarter. Atlanta rookie Zachariah Branch then lost his second fumble of the game on the ensuing kickoff, leading to Cairo Santos' 50-yard field goal to make it 31-7. Penix threw a 10-yard touchdown pass to Kyle Pitts Sr. with 9:34 remaining in the fourth, then hit Branch for a two-point conversion to cut the deficit to 31-15. Johnson lost a fumble on the next Chicago drive and Atlanta scored on Penix's 5-yard touchdown pass to Pitts with 5:41 left. Penix then found Drake London for another two-point conversion, slicing the Bears' lead to eight. After a Chicago punt, Kyler Gordon forced a Penix fumble for his third sack of the game. Devin Bush recovered at Atlanta's 28-yard line with 3:07 left. The Bears then picked up two first downs to ice the win. Williams fired a 14-yard touchdown strike to Colston Loveland to give the Bears an early 7-0 lead. On its second possession, Chicago doubled its lead on Swift's 4-yard rushing score. After Santos missed a 56-yard field goal with 7:19 left in the first half, Penix connected with London for a 39-yard pass to Chicago's 15-yard line. Penix then found Jahan Dotson for a 13-yard touchdown pass to pull the Falcons within seven. Atlanta forced a Chicago punt with 1:52 remaining, but Branch muffed the kick and Josh Blackwell recovered on the Falcons' 10-yard line. Three plays later, Swift rushed 2 yards for a touchdown to extend the lead to 21-7. Falcons rookie linebacker Kendal Daniels left the field on a stretcher in the third quarter. According to the Falcons, Daniels was conscious and had full movement of all extremities. He was taken to Grady Memorial Hospital in Atlanta for further evaluation. -Jack Batten, Field Level Media

item.title: Rubio afirma que Trump tardará hasta 60 días en valorar las sanciones a Rusia
item.description: Al día siguiente de suspender las sanciones y los aranceles relacionados con las exportaciones rusas, el presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, declaró el sábado que aún no ha anunciado una decisión definitiva al respecto, mientras que el secretario de Estado, Marco Rubio, afirmó que las autoridades necesitan más tiempo para evaluar la situación.
item.dc:creator: Nandita Bose, Gram Slattery
item.content:encoded: Al día siguiente de suspender las sanciones y los aranceles relacionados con las exportaciones rusas, el presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, declaró el sábado que aún no ha anunciado una decisión definitiva al respecto, mientras que el secretario de Estado, Marco Rubio, afirmó que las autoridades necesitan más tiempo para evaluar la situación. Rubio afirmó el sábado que el presidente se tomará hasta 60 días para evaluar el impacto económico de las sanciones y aranceles relacionados con Rusia que había suspendido el día anterior. "Muchos de ustedes aún no saben cuál es mi decisión, pero lo resolveremos y ustedes también se darán cuenta", declaró Trump a los periodistas en su club Mar-a-Lago, en Palm Beach, Florida. Trump firmó el viernes un decreto ejecutivo por el que suspendía sanciones y aranceles clave en virtud de la ley conocida como Ley Graham, que él mismo firmó el mes pasado a instancias de los legisladores que quieren presionar a Moscú por su guerra en Ucrania. Las medidas, que incluyen aranceles sobre los productos rusos y sanciones a los países que compren petróleo y gas rusos, debían entrar en vigor la próxima semana. La orden del viernes no especificaba cuánto duraría la exención, pero Rubio afirmó que Trump había optado por un periodo de revisión de 60 días. "Creo que el presidente quiere aprovechar este periodo de 60 días para analizar, en cierto modo, qué implicaciones tendrá la imposición tanto de sanciones como de aranceles para la economía mundial e incluso para la economía estadounidense", declaró Rubio a los periodistas antes de embarcar en un avión con destino a Uzbekistán. La orden ejecutiva del viernes suscitó críticas por parte del presidente ucraniano, Volodymyr Zelenskiy, quien advirtió de que envalentonaría al presidente ruso, Vladímir Putin, y prolongaría la guerra. SUMINISTROS DE DIÉSEL Rubio también defendió el sábado un acuerdo independiente de Estados Unidos con Rusia para aumentar el suministro de diésel a los mercados mundiales, con el objetivo de aliviar los precios del combustible, que se han disparado en medio de la guerra con Irán y las interrupciones en el suministro energético. "Ese diésel se va a vender de una forma u otra", afirmó Rubio. "La única diferencia es la cantidad que iban a recibir los Estados Unidos". Según el acuerdo, Trump afirmó que Rusia suministraría inicialmente más de 300 000 toneladas métricas de gasóleo a Estados Unidos, a las que seguirían envíos en noviembre y meses posteriores.

item.title: Rams CB Trent McDuffie (groin) inactive vs. Cardinals
item.description: Los Angeles Rams cornerback Trent McDuffie will not play against the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday because of a groin injury, in another blow to the team's defense.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Los Angeles Rams cornerback Trent McDuffie will not play against the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday because of a groin injury, in another blow to the team's defense. The Rams, who acquired the 2023 first-team All-Pro performer in an offseason trade with the Kansas City Chiefs, already have All-Pro pass rusher Myles Garrett (knee) on injured reserve. In his first season with the Rams, McDuffie, 26, has one interception and seven passes defended in five games (all starts). The injury for the Southern California native surfaced after practice Thursday. McDuffie had been listed as questionable to play along with safety Kam Curl (ankle), but Curl was listed as active for Sunday's game. After entering the season as the Super Bowl favorite, the Rams (2-3) are coming off a 37-34 overtime loss at home to the Buffalo Bills on Monday night. --Field Level Media

item.title: Titans erase Colts' 13-point lead to capture first win
item.description: Joey Slye connected on a tiebreaking 49-yard field goal with 2:03 left on Sunday as the visiting Tennessee Titans upset the Indianapolis Colts 26-20 for their first win of the season.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Joey Slye connected on a tiebreaking 49-yard field goal with 2:03 left on Sunday as the visiting Tennessee Titans upset the Indianapolis Colts 26-20 for their first win of the season. Slye finished with four field goals by adding a 44-yarder with 43 seconds remaining after Tennessee (1-5) got a fourth-down stop. The comeback from a 13-point halftime deficit gave head coach Robert Saleh his first win with the club. Cam Ward completed 11 of 22 passes for 102 yards with a touchdown and an interception for the Titans. Safety Amani Hooker finished with a career-high 13 tackles and an interception while Tennessee notched six sacks, including two apiece by Jeffery Simmons and Jermaine Johnson II. Daniel Jones hit 22 of 42 passes for 269 yards with one touchdown and two interceptions for Indianapolis (2-4) while Jonathan Taylor ran for 94 yards on 21 carries. That included a game-tying 4-yard touchdown with 5:32 to play. Tennessee entered the game as one of three winless teams in the NFL and played down to billing during the first half. After picking up three first downs on its opening drive before punting, it didn't get another one until the third quarter. By then, Indianapolis appeared to be in control with a 13-0 halftime lead. The Colts got into the end zone on their second possession via Jones' 1-yard touchdown pass to Mo Alie-Cox with 3:53 left in the second quarter. Later in the half, Spencer Shrader converted field goals of 23 and 47 yards -- the second coming after Ward tossed an interception. But Tennessee found its footing in the third quarter as Indianapolis committed one gaffe after another. Taylor's fumble teed up Slye's 29-yard field goal that got the Titans on the board with 13:30 left in the period. Slye bombed a 56-yarder following Jones' second interception. The Titans used special-teams magic to grab a fourth-quarter lead. Chimere Dike's 58-yard punt return to start the period set up Ward's 8-yard scoring strike to Carnell Tate. After getting a stop, Tennessee took a 20-13 lead when Julius Chestnut blocked Rigoberto Sanchez's punt and Oluwafemi Oladejo recovered for a 14-yard touchdown return with 10:17 remaining. --Field Level Media

item.title: Drake Maye throws 3 TD passes to get Patriots past Jets 26-19
item.description: Drake Maye tossed three touchdown passes and the New England Patriots extended their winning streak to three games with a 26-19 victory over the New York Jets on Sunday at Foxborough, Mass.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Drake Maye tossed three touchdown passes and the New England Patriots extended their winning streak to three games with a 26-19 victory over the New York Jets on Sunday at Foxborough, Mass. Maye completed 18 of 32 passes for 235 yards . Romeo Doubs, DeMario Douglas and Hunter Henry had New England's touchdown receptions, while Douglas caught seven passes for 86 yards. New York's Geno Smith completed 20 of 30 passes for 252 yards and a touchdown but was intercepted for the first time this season. The Jets (2-4) received four field goals from Jason Sanders and a game-high 11 tackles (six solo) from Jamien Sherwood. Sanders pulled the Jets within 26-19 by kicking a 36-yard field goal with 32 seconds to play, but New England (4-2) recovered the onside kick. After Sanders opened the scoring on a 42-yard field goal with 8:17 remaining in the first quarter, the Patriots scored the next 17 points to take a 17-3 halftime lead. New England took a 7-3 lead on a 42-yard touchdown pass from Maye to Doubs with 4:10 remaining in the first quarter, and added a 32-yard field goal by Andy Borregales that stretched the lead to 10-3 with 1:46 remaining in the second quarter. The advantage swelled to 17-3 after Douglas caught a 9-yard TD pass from Maye with 14 seconds left in the half. Smith's 48-yard touchdown pass to Omar Cooper Jr. helped slice New England's lead to 17-10 on New York's first drive of the second half. Following a TreVeyon Henderson fumble, Sanders connected on a 36-yard field goal that brought New York within 17-13 with 4:46 left in the third. The Patriots answered with a 7-yard TD pass from Maye to Henry, but the extra point was wide left from Borregales to leave New England with a 23-13 advantage 50 seconds into the fourth quarter. New York was within a touchdown after Sanders kicked a 40-yard field goal with 7:20 to play, but New England regained a 10-point lead when Borregales made a 27-yard field goal with 1:12 left. --Field Level Media

item.title: Browns get walk-off winner to catch Ravens in AFC North
item.description: Andre Szmyt kicked a 37-yard field goal as time expired to give the Cleveland Browns a 13-10 victory over the visiting Baltimore Ravens on Sunday and a share of first place in the AFC North.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Andre Szmyt kicked a 37-yard field goal as time expired to give the Cleveland Browns a 13-10 victory over the visiting Baltimore Ravens on Sunday and a share of first place in the AFC North. Deshaun Watson connected with Jerry Jeudy on a 33-yard pass to the Baltimore 29-yard line with 22 seconds remaining to set up the decisive kick. Szmyt's initial attempt from 42 yards was blocked by Keyon Martin, who was flagged for offside. Szmyt then drilled his second attempt through the uprights. Carson Schwesinger racked up 13 tackles and forced a fumble for the Browns (4-2), who are tied with the Ravens (4-2) and Pittsburgh Steelers (4-2) atop the division. The Steelers defeated the Tampa Bay Buccaneers 26-19 in overtime on Sunday. Audric Estime rushed for a touchdown five days after the Browns signed him off the Minnesota Vikings' practice squad with starter Quinshon Judkins (knee) ailing. Judkins was eventually ruled out of the contest. Watson was 16-of-26 passing for 164 yards as Cleveland halted a three-game slide against Baltimore. Tyler "Snoop" Huntley started for the Ravens in place of two-time NFL MVP Lamar Jackson (ankle) for the second straight week. He completed 19 of 31 passes for 165 yards and one touchdown. Josh Cuevas caught a scoring pass for Baltimore and Derrick Henry rushed for 58 yards on 17 carries but lost a key fumble. Cleveland trailed 10-0 at halftime before holding the ball for the first 7:12 of the third quarter and getting on the board when Szmyt booted a 48-yard field goal. Baltimore still led by seven when Tyler Loop was wide left on a 49-yard field-goal attempt with 14:13 left in the game. Less than two minutes later, the Ravens had the ball again and Henry was forced to fumble by Schwesinger. Tyson Campbell recovered the ball at the Ravens 35 with 12:36 left in the contest. Seven plays later, Estime scored on a 2-yard run to tie it 10-10 with 8:33 remaining. Cleveland had a chance to take the lead later in the quarter but Szmyt narrowly missed wide left from 48 yards with 3:40 remaining. That ended a streak of 25 straight makes for Szmyt dating to last season. The Ravens opened the game with an 11-play, 66-yard drive that featured Henry runs of 11 and 17 yards. The touchdown came when Cuevas was wide open in the middle of the end zone for a 2-yard reception from Huntley with 8:11 left in the opening quarter. Baltimore increased its lead to 10 when Loop connected on a 34-yard field goal with 4:37 remaining in the opening period. The Browns had just 46 yards and three first downs in the first half. --Field Level Media

item.title: Eagles lose edge Nolan Smith to concussion
item.description: Philadelphia Eagles edge rusher Nolan Smith exited the team's home game against the Carolina Panthers with a concussion and will not return, the team announced Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Philadelphia Eagles edge rusher Nolan Smith exited the team's home game against the Carolina Panthers with a concussion and will not return, the team announced Sunday. Smith, 25, was rushing the passer in the first half when he was chip-blocked by Carolina running back Chuba Hubbard. Smith fell to the ground and was checked for a concussion in the aftermath of the play. The Eagles (2-3) have dealt with a large number of key injuries this season. They entered the Carolina game missing quarterback Jalen Hurts and running back Saquon Barkley, among others. Smith recorded a first-half sack to bring his season total to three. That matches the 2025 total for the 2023 Eagles first-round draft pick. He now has 13.5 sacks for his career. --Field Level Media

item.title: Kenya confirms eighth Ebola case as regional outbreak spreads
item.description: Kenya has confirmed one more Ebola case, bringing the total number of infections in the country to eight, Director-General for Health Patrick Amoth said on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Kenya has confirmed one more Ebola case, bringing the total number of infections in the country to eight, Director-General for Health Patrick Amoth said on Sunday. "Today, 38 people were tested, and one tested positive for Ebola," Amoth said in an interview on Kenya's Citizen TV. "He is a 49-year-old man who is not a healthcare worker. He developed fever, headache and muscle pain." Amoth said the new case was a patient attendant who cleaned utensils and linens, and he was probably exposed to Kenya's first Ebola case, discovered earlier this month, in a man who travelled from Democratic Republic of Congo to Nairobi and died at a Nairobi hospital on October 5. The latest case developed symptoms on Saturday, was separated from other people in quarantine, and was tested for the virus with the result returning positive on Sunday, a health ministry source said. Kenya has been on heightened alert, as a major [USN:L1N46401K TEXT:"Ebola outbreak centered"] in Congo has spread across borders in the region. [USN:L1N46401K TEXT:"Congo confirmed"] on Sunday that its outbreak had spread to an eighth province, North Ubangi, underscoring concerns about wider regional transmission.

item.title: Falcons rookie LB Kendal Daniels carted off after tackle vs. Bears
item.description: Atlanta Falcons rookie linebacker Kendal Daniels left the field on a stretcher following a lengthy delay in the third quarter of Sunday's game against the visiting Chicago Bears.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Atlanta Falcons rookie linebacker Kendal Daniels left the field on a stretcher following a lengthy delay in the third quarter of Sunday's game against the visiting Chicago Bears. According to the Falcons, Daniels was conscious and had full movement of all extremities. He was taken to Grady Memorial Hospital in Atlanta for further evaluation. Daniels, 23, stumbled into a low tackle on Chicago tight end Colston Loveland, then rolled over while putting his face toward the turf. He remained motionless for several minutes as medical personnel attended to him. The fourth-round draft pick last April out of Oklahoma has started on defense in each of his first six NFL games. Daniels entered Sunday with one sack among his 22 tackles and had seven tackles against the Bears before departing. --Field Level Media

item.title: Rangers seek power-play improvement as Ducks visit
item.description: The New York Rangers hope they can effectively convert their power-play chances, avoid a third straight loss and stay unbeaten at home Monday night when they play host to the Anaheim Ducks.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The New York Rangers hope they can effectively convert their power-play chances, avoid a third straight loss and stay unbeaten at home Monday night when they play host to the Anaheim Ducks. The Rangers are around NHL average in power-play effectiveness, but there have been missed opportunities of late. New York's power play is 6-for-30, and its 20% success rate was tied for 16th in the 32-team NHL heading into Sunday's games. The Rangers have drawn at least three power-play opportunities in seven of their first 10 games. After absorbing a 7-1 loss at the New Jersey Devils on Thursday, the Rangers fell 1-0 in overtime to the Columbus Blue Jackets on Saturday. Before New York rookie goalie Dylan Garand was beaten by the Blue Jackets' Kent Johnson for the game winner, the Rangers were scoreless on three power-play chances versus a team that allowed four power-play goals Tuesday against the Florida Panthers. All three power-play chances Saturday were in the opening 12 minutes of the third period. Four of their 29 shots came on their man advantages. "I don't think we got in as clean," New York's J.T. Miller said after being denied on a tip-in during the first power play and missing on the same play during the second advantage. "We didn't come up with the contested pucks in the corners. I felt like they did. "So it wasn't our best, and we, to a man, understand that you get three power plays in the third, nothing-nothing on the road, you have to step up there." The Rangers return from their two-game trip seeking their first 6-0-0 start on home ice since winning their first eight home games in 1990-91. The Rangers started 0-6-1 at home last season and did not get their sixth home win until beating the Boston Bruins on Jan. 26. Anaheim will play seven of its next 10 on the road and starts a four-game trip following consecutive 4-2 home losses to the Calgary Flames and Bruins. The Ducks allowed a combined five goals in the third period of those games, which includes two of the three power-play goals the Bruins earned on Friday. Tim Washe and Beckett Sennecke scored 21 seconds apart in the final minute of the opening period against the Bruins, but the Ducks went scoreless on five power plays. Anaheim saw its penalty kill falter after opponents were 0-for-10 on power plays in the previous three games and 2-for-21 in the first six games. "We really have to watch some film and learn how to play with the lead," said Anaheim forward Nikita Nesterenko. "Obviously, that's a couple games now with Edmonton and Calgary, so it's about learning from it." The disappointing special-teams performance occurred on a night when the Ducks conceded 22 shots on goal after permitting a season-high 36 against the Flames. The Ducks are hoping for more shot blocks after getting seven against the Bruins and a vastly improved performance in the faceoff circle after losing 40 of 58 faceoffs. Anaheim played Friday without Mikael Granlund due to a lower-body injury. He is considered day to day but practiced on Saturday ahead of the East Coast trip. The Ducks swept the season series in 2025-26 and are seeking four straight victories over the Rangers for the first time. --Field Level Media

item.title: Anthropic destinará 5% de suas ações a novo fundo de benefício público
item.description: A Anthropic anunciou neste domingo que destinará 5% de suas ações a um novo fundo de benefício público, sujeito à aprovação dos acionistas, com a participação podendo aumentar à medida que a avaliação da gigante da inteligência artificial aumentar.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A Anthropic anunciou neste domingo que destinará 5% de suas ações a um novo fundo de benefício público, sujeito à aprovação dos acionistas, com a participação podendo aumentar à medida que a avaliação da gigante da inteligência artificial aumentar. O fundo proposto seria constituído como uma sociedade de responsabilidade limitada de propriedade integral e receberia mais 2% das ações da Anthropic, a critério do conselho, para cada aumento de 50% no valor da empresa acima de um valor de referência que ainda não foi divulgado. O Fundo de Benefício Público da Anthropic poderia apoiar iniciativas que incluem doações a organizações sem fins lucrativos, distribuições diretas a populações específicas e esforços para lidar com o impacto da IA sobre os trabalhadores. A empresa afirmou que nenhuma parte do patrimônio detido pelo fundo seria utilizada para atividades de lobby ou contribuições políticas nos EUA ou no exterior. A fabricante do assistente de IA Claude está planejando uma das maiores ofertas públicas iniciais (IPO) da história como uma [USN:L6N45L0UH TEXT:"corporação de benefício público"], uma estrutura jurídica que exige que a administração leve em consideração certos interesses mais amplos, além de gerar lucro para os investidores. A empresa, que se posicionou com a segurança em primeiro lugar, tem frequentemente destacado os riscos associados aos seus modelos de IA, mais recentemente em seu [USN:L4N45K1J5 TEXT:"prospecto de IPO"], no qual afirmou que eles poderiam exibir “comportamentos de autopreservação”, conforme reportagem exclusiva da Reuters em setembro. Somado ao novo fundo, cerca de 20% das ações da Anthropic seriam destinadas a fins públicos, excluindo quaisquer ações adicionais que possam ser alocadas caso a empresa atinja marcos futuros de avaliação. A Anthropic afirmou que divulgará mais detalhes nos próximos meses sobre a governança do fundo, sua estrutura e os limites de avaliação que poderiam ampliar sua participação acionária. A empresa também planeja publicar um relatório de benefício público detalhando o progresso em direção à sua missão. (Reportagem de Abu Sultan e Anusha Shah em Bengaluru)

item.title: Reuniões do FMI e Banco Mundial deixam países em desenvolvimento com mais perguntas do que respostas
item.description: As reuniões do Fundo Monetário Internacional e do Banco Mundial na semana passada não trouxeram novas respostas para o mundo em desenvolvimento em relação às questões levantadas pela guerra que se alastra no Oriente Médio, pela guerra que persiste na Ucrânia, pelo aumento dos custos de dívida e por uma possível bolha da IA.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Shalal, David Lawder
item.content:encoded: As reuniões do Fundo Monetário Internacional e do Banco Mundial na semana passada não trouxeram novas respostas para o mundo em desenvolvimento em relação às questões levantadas pela guerra que se alastra no Oriente Médio, pela guerra que persiste na Ucrânia, pelo aumento dos custos de dívida e por uma possível bolha da IA. Não é a primeira vez que [USN:L1N46302K TEXT:"os países de baixa renda"] são abalados pelas repercussões das ações das nações mais ricas: aumento dos custos do serviço da dívida, inflação mais elevada e o risco de ficarem cada vez mais para trás economicamente devido ao boom da IA. O que receberam foram os conselhos de sempre que os credores globais costumam dar: reduzir os déficits fiscais e acelerar as reformas econômicas para atrair mais investimentos do setor privado. Kristalina Georgieva, a primeira diretora-geral do FMI proveniente de um país em desenvolvimento -- a Bulgária --, afirmou que as economias avançadas são, na verdade, as maiores responsáveis pelos desequilíbrios orçamentários. Ela observou que os níveis de endividamento dos países em desenvolvimento haviam, na verdade, caído nos últimos anos, mas que o aumento dos rendimentos dos títulos em outros lugares elevou os custos de endividamento. Os pagamentos médios do serviço da dívida nesses países mais que dobraram em relação a uma década atrás, chegando a 14% da receita governamental, prejudicando a educação, a saúde e outras áreas essenciais, disse ela. ECONOMIAS AVANÇADAS FOCADAS EM SEUS PRÓPRIOS PROBLEMAS Em um painel no sábado, Georgieva disse que muitas questões continuavam sem solução, especialmente em relação à IA: “Estamos em uma situação em que temos muito mais perguntas do que respostas. E meu alerta a todos é: não se deixem enganar por quem finge ter as respostas. Eles estão enganando vocês.” Josh Lipsky, vice-presidente de economia internacional do think tank Atlantic Council, disse que as reuniões perderam a oportunidade de apresentar orientações ou formas de ajudar. “É difícil falar sobre o mundo em desenvolvimento quando as economias avançadas não estão organizadas e correm o risco de uma crise fiscal”, disse ele. “E isso se soma às situações políticas em muitos desses países, o que faz com que a ajuda ao desenvolvimento não seja uma prioridade no momento.” Mauricio Cárdenas, ex-ministro da Fazenda da Colômbia e atualmente pesquisador da Escola de Relações Internacionais e Assuntos Públicos da Universidade de Columbia, em Nova York, disse que muitos formuladores de políticas ficaram com a profunda sensação de que “algo realmente ruim poderia acontecer”, mas sem um roteiro concreto para traçar o caminho no futuro. “O FMI e o Banco Mundial não estão particularmente bem preparados para essa nova fase. Eles entendem que algo está acontecendo, trazem especialistas em IA”, disse ele. “Mas, no fim das contas, não há nenhum tipo de orientação específica e concreta sobre como se preparar para algo cuja evolução ainda é difícil de entender." As tensões geopolíticas que têm abalado ambas as instituições desde a invasão da Ucrânia pela Rússia em 2022, complicando ações coordenadas, também ficaram evidentes em Bangcoc, quando quase metade dos delegados de um [USN:L1N46301V TEXT:"comitê diretor do FMI"] abandonou a sala durante a intervenção do ministro das Finanças da Rússia. Os ataques houthis ao aeroporto de Riade atrasaram a chegada do chefe desse comitê, o ministro das Finanças da Arábia Saudita, Mohammed Al-Jadaan, que teve que viajar por terra até o Catar para embarcar em um voo. E a própria Bangcoc serviu como um forte lembrete dos desafios enfrentados pelos países em desenvolvimento, ainda parcialmente alagada após as enchentes de setembro que causaram quase US$200 milhões em prejuízos ao setor industrial da Tailândia. AUMENTO DA DESIGUALDADE PODE ELEVAR CUSTOS A LONGO PRAZO Kate Pickett, professora da Universidade de York, instou os formuladores de políticas a se concentrarem em um crescimento mais inclusivo, em vez de forçar os países em desenvolvimento a adotarem reformas estruturais rigorosas. “Se a desigualdade aumentar, se a pobreza se agravar, isso aumentará seus custos a longo prazo”, disse ela. “Não basta descrever uma economia como resiliente. Ela só é resiliente para os ricos e os privilegiados.” Ayhan Kose, economista-chefe adjunto do Banco Mundial, disse que a economia global resistiu ao seu maior choque energético -- decorrente da guerra dos EUA e de Israel contra o Irã -- melhor do que o esperado. Mas, embora uma recessão global tenha sido evitada, ele disse que as perspectivas de crescimento, tanto nas economias em desenvolvimento quanto nas avançadas, estavam piores do que antes. O crescimento já havia caído na metade das economias avançadas, enquanto nos países em desenvolvimento como um todo, ele desacelerou significativamente, passando de 4,4% para perto de 3,6%. “As pessoas estão realmente preocupadas porque a resiliência de hoje não é garantia de resiliência amanhã”, disse ele. “Agora, elas estão preocupadas com qual será o próximo choque, pois a cada seis meses, se não a cada três meses, surge um novo choque.” Embora nenhuma iniciativa específica tenha sido anunciada, ele disse que o Banco Mundial continua focado em ajudar os países em desenvolvimento a se prepararem para os avanços em IA, em parte por meio da mobilização de mais capital privado, que agora é o triplo dos níveis de 2022. No entanto, o Banco Mundial também precisa lidar com quedas acentuadas na ajuda oficial ao desenvolvimento e com desafios persistentes para atrair investimento estrangeiro para os países em desenvolvimento. (Reportagem de Andrea Shalal e David Lawder; reportagem adicional de Rae Wee)

item.title: Macron condemns "shocking" scenes of violence across France
item.description: French President Emmanuel Macron condemned on Sunday what he called the "dissenters" who looted and vandalised cities in "shocking" scenes across France on the sidelines of protests over the cost of living.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: French President Emmanuel Macron condemned on Sunday what he called the "dissenters" who looted and vandalised cities in "shocking" scenes across France on the sidelines of protests over the cost of living. "Looking at these images, we have all asked ourselves: what was going through their minds? How can French people do this to France?" Macron said in a televised address to the nation. "Nothing justifies it, nothing explains it, nothing excuses it. Tonight, we all feel anger and shame." Macron, whose final six months in office are being shaped by mounting political, fiscal and social pressures, said he had ordered a review to determine whether there had been failings in intelligence gathering or police preparedness before protests that were later marred by looting and violence. He said prefects and mayors would be empowered to ban certain gatherings where necessary. Macron also said he had asked the government to bring together students, teachers, lawmakers, trade union representatives and business leaders this week to formulate what he described as "concrete proposals" to address the crisis, without providing further details. "We must sit around the table and build solutions together," he said.

item.title: Slow-starting Arsenal make patience pay against Forest
item.description: Arsenal are gaining a reputation as slow starters this season, but their ability to find a way through tight games helped them earn a 1-0 win against Nottingham Forest on Sunday and keep their Premier League title defence on track.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Arsenal are gaining a reputation as slow starters this season, but their ability to find a way through tight games helped them earn a 1-0 win against Nottingham Forest on Sunday and keep their Premier League title defence on track. Arsenal's total of 11 league goals from seven games is the second-lowest in the top six, eight behind leaders Manchester City and a whopping 12 behind third-placed Brighton & Hove Albion. Eight of those 11 strikes have come after halftime and they again struggled for attacking fluency in the opening 45 minutes against Forest before substitute Noni Madueke's deflected 80th-minute strike secured the points. The goal came from Arsenal's first shot on target and kept Mikel Arteta's side in touch with table-toppers City. "The longer the game goes on, they have more belief. You have to take more risks, and that's when the game can break," an upbeat Arteta told Sky Sports. Madueke said Arsenal might not have won such a game last season but now possessed greater belief and resilience. "At times maybe last year, this game might have not gone as it did for us in the end, but I think we got that extra belief, that extra mentality now," he said. "We know we're the champions, and we know we can pull out the bag wherever we go, and just delighted that we're able to do it today." Arsenal looked toothless in the first half and although they were sharper after the break, it still took until the 80th minute for Madueke to produce the effort that finally broke the hosts' resistance. The 24-year-old, who came off the bench at the break to replace Eberechi Eze, said Arsenal's squad depth was proving to be one of their main strengths this season. "If you look at the quality of our starting 11 and bench it's absurd, so we know that we're going to start some and finish some (games) and for me it's the same mentality every time, I just want to create or score. Amazing feeling (to score), but I feel better about the win," he said. "We have elite players, all 20-something players are elite and of the highest level. It's great to have that type of competition, you know on the bench you're ready to have an impact."

item.title: France Macron dit vouloir punir les "casseurs" et écouter les manifestants
item.description: Emmanuel Macron a fait dimanche la distinction entre les "casseurs" et les manifestants aux "revendications légitimes", invitant le gouvernement à faire en sorte que le chaos constaté la veille "ne puisse pas se reproduire".
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Emmanuel Macron a fait dimanche la distinction entre les "casseurs" et les manifestants aux "revendications légitimes", invitant le gouvernement à faire en sorte que le chaos constaté la veille "ne puisse pas se reproduire". "Notre responsabilité est double : entendre la colère et agir sur ses causes, et faire respecter fermement l'ordre républicain. Nous ne devons ni confondre les revendications légitimes avec la violence, ni laisser les violences empêcher que ces revendications soient entendues", a dit le président lors d'une allocution à l'Elysée. Le chef de l'Etat a réuni dimanche après-midi le Premier ministre, Sébastien Lecornu, et les ministres concernés par les manifestations de la veille qui ont été émaillées d'affrontements, de destructions de bâtiments publics et de pillages dans tout le pays. Plusieurs centaines de policiers ont été blessés et près de 2.400 individus ont été interpellés, selon le ministère de l'Intérieur. "Des factieux issus de groupuscules d'ultra-gauche rejoints par de nombreux délinquants se sont livrés à une violence débridées dans nos villes", a dit Emmanuel Macron. "Rien de le justifie, rien de l'explique, rien ne l'excuse", a-t-il poursuivi, annonçant pour ce lundi une "cellule de crise" présidée par Sébastien Lecornu "pour mobiliser les aides les plus rapides". Les maires de Paris, Lyon et Marseille et une partie de l'opposition ont critiqué la gestion du maintien de l'ordre par l'exécutif. "Nos forces de l'ordre, malgré leur professionnalisme ont eu à subir une violence inouïe", a dit Emmanuel Macron. "J'ai demandé au gouvernement d'en tirer toutes les leçons en terme de renseignement et d'anticipation et faire en sorte que cela ne puisse pas se reproduire. J'attends des réponses claires et toute la transparence sera faite." "CEUX QUI ONT DÉTRUIT DOIVENT PAYER" Pour prévenir tout nouveau débordement, Emmanuel Macron a demandé aux préfets de prendre des décisions "en lien avec les maires" allant "jusqu'à interdire certains rassemblements". Il a aussi appelé "l'ensemble des partis politiques, des organisations professionnelles et syndicales", prochainement réunis par le Premier ministre, "à condamner sans ambiguïté toutes les violences et à appeler au calme". "Le pays a besoin d'ordre, d'apaisement et pas d'une escalade", a-t-il considéré à six mois d'une élection présidentielle pour laquelle "nous avons besoin d'unité de calme et de respect". Emmanuel Macron s'est adressé sans la nommer à La France insoumise de Jean-Luc Mélenchon, accusée par le Premier ministre et une partie de la classe politique d'encourager les manifestations violentes. "Tous ceux qui vous expliquent que l'urgence est de manifester et d'aller dans la rue n'ont qu'un but : abîmer la République et voler le débat", a dit Emmanuel Macron. Pour ce qui est des responsables des violences, "ceux qui ont détruit doivent payer, ceux qui ont pillé doivent rembourser, ceux qui ont cherché à faire tomber la République auront à en répondre" a dit le président. Emmanuel Macron s'est aussi adressé aux manifestants qui ont défilé par centaines de milliers samedi contre la vie chère et la situation dans les lycées et les universités, notamment. "Jamais nous ne devons confondre ces derniers avec ceux qui ont détruit, cassé, pillé", a-t-il dit. Evoquant les jeunes qui manifestent depuis des semaines, le président a estimé que "leur parole doit être entendue, sans a priori et sans minimiser les difficultés". Emmanuel Macron doit effectuer en début de semaine une tournée au Proche-Orient qui le conduira au Koweït, aux Emirats arabes unis, à Bahreïn et au Qatar. Le chef de l'Etat n'a pas changé son programme malgré la situation en France, a fait savoir son entourage.

item.title: McLaren vai vender cinco carros de F1, todos pilotados por campeões e um por Brad Pitt
item.description: A McLaren está vendendo cinco carros de Fórmula 1 em pleno funcionamento, pilotados por campeões, incluindo Lewis Hamilton e o falecido Ayrton Senna, sendo que um deles também foi testado pelo ator de Hollywood Brad Pitt.
item.dc:creator: Alan Baldwin
item.content:encoded: A McLaren está vendendo cinco carros de Fórmula 1 em pleno funcionamento, pilotados por campeões, incluindo Lewis Hamilton e o falecido Ayrton Senna, sendo que um deles também foi testado pelo ator de Hollywood Brad Pitt. Os carros, que serão vendidos por meio do revendedor de luxo Tom Hartley Jr. e devem arrecadar dezenas de milhões de dólares, serão preparados pela atual campeã do campeonato de construtores para seus próximos proprietários. Hartley Jr. também vendeu a coleção do [USN:L3N3PQ0Q7 TEXT:"ex-chefe da F1 Bernie Ecclestone"] e 20 carros de passeio que pertenciam ao falecido coproprietário da McLaren, [USN:L4N3UJ12T TEXT:"Mansour Ojjeh."] “Decidimos nos desfazer desses icônicos carros de Fórmula 1 da McLaren porque achamos que mantê-los simplesmente guardados em um depósito é um desserviço ao que eles representam”, disse o presidente-executivo da McLaren Racing, Zak Brown, em comunicado divulgado neste domingo. “Esses carros foram construídos para serem dirigidos e competir, e queremos vê-los sendo usados e apreciados. Acreditamos que essa seja a melhor maneira de manter viva nossa história e ativo nosso negócio de patrimônio.” PITT DIRIGIU UM DELES APÓS FILMAGENS DE FILME Os cinco carros abrangem 32 anos da história da McLaren, começando com dois carros MP4/6A (chassis números 04 e 07 com motores Honda V12) pilotados pelo austríaco Gerhard Berger e testados por Senna durante a campanha que resultou no título de 1991. O chassi 04 ficou em segundo lugar em uma dobradinha no Grande Prêmio de San Marino, com as McLaren dando voltas à frente de todo o pelotão. O chassi 07 ficou em segundo lugar no Grande Prêmio da Inglaterra, corrida realizada em casa para a McLaren. Ambos estão na posse da McLaren desde então. Um McLaren MP4/27A de 2012 (chassi 01), pilotado pelo campeão mundial de 2009, Jenson Button, e testado pelo heptacampeão mundial Hamilton, também está à venda. Dois carros pilotados exclusivamente pelo atual campeão Lando Norris em 2021 e 2023 completam o lote. O McLaren MCL35M de 2021 levou Norris ao pódio em Ímola, Mônaco e Monza, enquanto o MCL37A-03 de 2023 venceu corridas consecutivas em Cingapura e no Japão e foi testado após o fim da temporada por um grupo de pilotos, incluindo o companheiro de equipe de Norris, Oscar Piastri, e Mick Schumacher, filho do grande Michael da F1. O McLaren de 2023 foi pilotado por Pitt em um teste privado no Circuito das Américas, em Austin, em junho do ano passado, em conexão com seu papel de protagonista no filme “F1: O Filme”, e é o carro de F1 mais moderno oferecido à venda para um proprietário particular. Pitt teria atingido uma velocidade de 197 mph (317 km/h) com o carro. “É extremamente raro que um colecionador tenha a oportunidade de adquirir carros de Grande Prêmio que participaram de corridas diretamente do fabricante e da equipe que os construíram e competiram com eles, e isso torna esta uma oferta muito especial”, disse Hartley. “Esses cinco carros serão oferecidos individualmente e não há qualquer pressão de tempo. Nossa prioridade, e a da McLaren, é encontrar os donos certos para eles.” Embora nenhum preço tenha sido divulgado, espera-se que os valores variem de 5 milhões de libras (US$6,7 milhões) a até 10 milhões. Um McLaren MP4-25A pilotado por Hamilton na vitória na Turquia em 2010 foi vendido por 4,8 milhões de libras em 2021, enquanto uma Ferrari vencedora de 2001, pilotada por Michael Schumacher, alcançou US$ 7,5 milhões em Nova York em 2017. (Reportagem de Alan Baldwin)

item.title: Anthropic to commit 5% stake to new public benefit fund
item.description: Anthropic said on Sunday it will commit 5% of its shares to a new public benefit fund, subject to stockholder approval, with the stake potentially increasing as the artificial intelligence giant's valuation grows.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Anthropic said on Sunday it will commit 5% of its shares to a new public benefit fund, subject to stockholder approval, with the stake potentially increasing as the artificial intelligence giant's valuation grows. The proposed fund would be established as a wholly owned limited liability company and would receive an additional 2% of Anthropic's shares, at the board's discretion, for every 50% increase in the company's value above a baseline that has yet to be disclosed. The Anthropic Public Benefit Fund could support initiatives including nonprofit donations, direct distributions to specific populations and efforts to address AI’s impact on workers. The company said none of the equity held by the fund would be used for lobbying or political contributions in the US or abroad. The maker of the Claude AI assistant is planning one of the biggest IPOs in history as a [USN:L6N45L0UH TEXT:"public benefit corporation"], a legal structure that requires management to consider certain broader interests as well as turning a profit for investors. The company, which has positioned itself as safety-first, has often highlighted risks associated with its AI models, most recently in its [USN:L4N45K1J5 TEXT:"IPO prospectus"], which it said could exhibit "self-preserving behaviors," Reuters reported exclusively in September. Taken together with the new fund, roughly 20% of Anthropic's shares would be dedicated to public purposes, excluding any additional shares that could be allocated if it reaches future valuation milestones. Anthropic said it would disclose further details in coming months on the fund's governance, structure and the valuation thresholds that could expand its ownership stake. It also plans to publish a public-benefit report detailing progress toward its mission.

item.title: Wake Forest baseball coach Tom Walter placed on leave
item.description: Wake Forest has placed longtime baseball coach Tom Walter on leave, the university confirmed.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Wake Forest has placed longtime baseball coach Tom Walter on leave, the university confirmed. The school issued a statement Saturday after Wake Forest-centered site Demon Deacons Digest reported the news. No reason for the move has been disclosed. "Wake Forest baseball head coach Tom Walter is on leave effective October 14, 2026," spokesperson Ryan Madden told the outlet. "Additional information will be shared when it becomes appropriate. In accordance with University policy Wake Forest Athletics will have no further comment at this time." Eric Niesen, an assistant coach on the pitching side, currently is in charge of the program, with an assist from administrator Craig Zakrzewski. Before returning to his alma mater as a coach before the 2026 season, Niesen served as director of pitching for the Houston Astros. Walter began as the Demon Deacons' head coach in June 2009. The program made a fifth consecutive appearance in the NCAA Tournament in 2026 and reached the Men's College World Series in 2023. Chase Burns, Nick Kurtz, Gavin Sheets and Rhett Lowder are among the current major leaguers to have played for Walter. Walter was in the news in June 2025 after he appeared to utter a homophobic slur as his team lost to Tennessee in the NCAA Knoxville Regional. Video of the incident spread, and Walter apologized the next day. Athletic director John Currie called the conduct "disappointing" in a public rebuke. Walter has 536 career wins at Wake Forest. He owns a career record of 964-738-1 that includes his years as head coach at George Washington (1997-2004) and New Orleans (2005-09). He became the seventh coach to lead three programs to the NCAA Tournament at the Division I level. --Field Level Media

item.title: Report: Saints QB Tyler Shough playing with broken bones in left hand
item.description: New Orleans Saints quarterback Tyler Shough will once again be under center on Sunday against the New York Giants while playing with multiple broken bones in his non-throwing hand, ESPN reported.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: New Orleans Saints quarterback Tyler Shough will once again be under center on Sunday against the New York Giants while playing with multiple broken bones in his non-throwing hand, ESPN reported. The Saints have listed Shough on the injury report with a hand injury, but the specifics have not been revealed by the team. He has continued to play through the injury that reportedly occurred in the Saints' 45-24 loss to the Atlanta Falcons on Oct. 5. Shough has played with his ring and pinky fingers taped together while wearing a protective glove. It has not impacted his ability to pass the ball and he has completed handoffs on running plays with his right throwing hand. The injury is expected to take multiple months to fully heal, according to the report, with New Orleans set to go on its bye week after playing the Pittsburgh Steelers next Sunday in Paris. Shough, 27, has completed 66.8% of his passes for 1,299 yards and nine touchdowns with five interceptions as the Saints carried a 1-4 record into Sunday's game against the Giants. In two NFL seasons, the Saints' 2025 second-round draft pick has completed 67.3% of his passes for 3,683 yards, 19 touchdowns and 11 interceptions in 16 games, while New Orleans has gone 6-8 in his 14 starts. --Field Level Media

item.title: Brighton's patience pays off as Huerzeler helps Seagulls soar
item.description: Eight months after some Brighton & Hove Albion fans called for Fabian Huerzeler to be sacked after a home defeat by Crystal Palace, the young manager has the Seagulls soaring in third place in the Premier League after Sunday's 5-0 rout of the same opponents.
item.dc:creator: Rohith Nair
item.content:encoded: Eight months after some Brighton & Hove Albion fans called for Fabian Huerzeler to be sacked after a home defeat by Crystal Palace, the young manager has the Seagulls soaring in third place in the Premier League after Sunday's 5-0 rout of the same opponents. The 33-year-old, the youngest manager in the English top flight, watched his side demolish rivals Palace in a game capped by [USN:L4N464024 TEXT:"Diego Gomez's spectacular halfway-line strike"] that sent the home fans into raptures. It was a far cry from February's 1-0 defeat in the "M23 Derby" that left Brighton languishing in 14th place as some of the club's fans chanted "You're getting sacked in the morning." Brighton, however, refused to push the panic button and retained their faith in Huerzeler, who eventually guided the south-coast club to an eighth-placed finish. Chairman Tony Bloom [USN:L1N41K15A TEXT:"rewarded Huerzeler with a contract extension"] until 2029 and the club are reaping the benefits of the trust placed in the young German. LEAGUE-LEADING 23 GOALS With Sunday's 5-0 victory, Brighton sit five points behind leaders Manchester City with a league-leading 23 goals in seven games, five clean sheets and a goal difference of plus 18, six better than City's. "A few months ago (after losing to Palace) we were in a different place and I said I'd keep pushing to get another opportunity to beat them, so I'm happy we did it today," Huerzeler told Sky Sports. "It's not a one-man show, so I credit my players and my staff. Hopefully everyone enjoyed it." While Erling Haaland has scored eight of City's goals to move clear in the Golden Boot race, Brighton have already had 11 different scorers. "If you look, they're shared around a lot which is a massive help. We've got everyone chipping in and helping out the team," Brighton defender Lewis Dunk told BBC Radio. "If you look at our clean sheets, I think it's the most we've ever had at this part of the season, so we're buzzing with that as well." RELENTLESS PRESSING Brighton's success in the new campaign has been built on relentless pressing, a hallmark of last month's commanding 3-0 victory over champions Arsenal that left coach [USN:L6N45B053 TEXT:"Mikel Arteta searching for answers"] after his side's first defeat of the season. Pascal Gross's successful return has provided another major boost. The 35-year-old, who previously spent seven seasons at Brighton, rejoined the club earlier this year in search of regular first-team football. Gross is their joint-top scorer with three goals while the German also leads the team with four assists. It was his free kick that forced an own goal in the fourth minute that opened the floodgates against Palace. Dunk refused to entertain talk of a title challenge so early in the season, while Huerzeler was equally determined to keep expectations in check. "To me, the most important thing is the things we can improve... It's good to celebrate the win, but understand there is still space for improvement, especially for individual players," he said. "We have to keep going. We can't be satisfied. We have to keep pushing, stay humble and understand why we are successful at the moment to keep pushing at that level."

item.title: Trump says Washington golf course renovation to start in November, despite judge's order
item.description: US President Donald Trump said on Sunday that his administration would begin renovation work next month on a historic Washington golf course that a federal judge had ordered could not proceed without prior court notification.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: US President Donald Trump said on Sunday that his administration would begin renovation work next month on a historic Washington golf course that a federal judge had ordered could not proceed without prior court notification. The renovation work, which Trump earlier this year had said [USN:L1N43005N TEXT:"would begin in September"], has become the subject of a lawsuit over environmental and historic preservation concerns. Trump said in a post on Truth Social that work on the East Potomac Golf Links would begin on November 15 and that it would reopen in about 15 months. The renovation is among [USN:L6N41H110 TEXT:"a number of projects"] Trump is pursuing to reshape the White House and other Washington landmarks. US District Judge Ana Reyes ruled earlier this year that the government must give notice before any substantive construction work on the golf course could proceed, and last week [USN:L1N45Y0L4 TEXT:"issued an order"] halting the removal of trees at the site, which she called "inexcusable." The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment on whether Trump's announcement on Sunday would conflict with Reyes' directives. The DC Preservation League brought a lawsuit in February to halt the administration's takeover of the golf course, alleging that it would violate environmental laws and "irreparably destroy a priceless piece of American history." In an October 9 court filing, the Trump administration had asked Reyes to dismiss the litigation, saying it was premature because the "proposed project remains at an early and conceptual stage." The following day, however, the government removed about 500 trees from the site, which it said would improve safety at the park and restore its original design, and was part of a 2019 plan that predates Trump's ambitions for the course. Reyes ordered a halt to the removals. On Friday, the government filed a motion to disqualify Reyes and move the case to another district judge, saying her actions had shown "deep-seated and unequivocal antipathy toward the Trump Administration," according to court records.

item.title: McLaren to sell five F1 cars, all driven by champions and one by Brad Pitt
item.description: McLaren are selling five fully-functioning Formula One cars driven by champions, including Lewis Hamilton and the late Brazilian Ayrton Senna, with one also tested by Hollywood actor Brad Pitt.
item.dc:creator: Alan Baldwin
item.content:encoded: McLaren are selling five fully-functioning Formula One cars driven by champions, including Lewis Hamilton and the late Brazilian Ayrton Senna, with one also tested by Hollywood actor Brad Pitt. The cars, to be sold through high-end dealer Tom Hartley Jr. and expected to raise tens of millions of dollars, will be prepared by the reigning constructors' champions for their next owners. Hartley Jr. also sold the collection of [USN:L3N3PQ0Q7 TEXT:"former F1 supremo Bernie Ecclestone"] and 20 road cars belonging to the late McLaren co-owner [USN:L4N3UJ12T TEXT:"Mansour Ojjeh."] "We have decided to part with these iconic McLaren Formula One cars because we feel that having them simply sitting in storage is a disservice to what they represent," McLaren Racing CEO Zak Brown said in a statement on Sunday. "These cars were built to be driven and raced, and we want to see them being used and enjoyed. We believe that is the best way to keep our history alive and our heritage business active." PITT DROVE ONE AFTER FILMING F1 MOVIE The five span 32 years of McLaren history, starting with two MP4/6A cars (chassis numbers 04 and 07 with Honda V12 engines) raced by Austrian Gerhard Berger and tested by Senna during the 1991 title-winning campaign. Chassis 04 finished second in a one-two at the San Marino Grand Prix with the McLarens lapping the entire field. Chassis 07 came second at McLaren's home British Grand Prix. Both have been in McLaren's possession ever since. A 2012 McLaren MP4/27A (chassis 01) raced by 2009 world champion Jenson Button and tested by seven-times world champion Hamilton is also for sale. Two cars raced exclusively by reigning champion Lando Norris in 2021 and 2023 complete the group. The 2021 McLaren MCL35M took Norris to the podium in Imola, Monaco and Monza while the 2023 MCL37A-03 won successive races in Singapore and Japan and was tested post-season by a roster of drivers including Norris's teammate Oscar Piastri and Mick Schumacher, son of F1 great Michael. The 2023 McLaren was driven by Pitt in a private test at Austin's Circuit of the Americas in June last year in connection with his starring role in "F1 the Movie" and is the most modern F1 car offered for sale to a private owner. Pitt reportedly took it up to a speed of 197mph (317kph). "It is incredibly rare for a collector to have the opportunity to acquire race-driven Grand Prix cars directly from the manufacturer and team that built and campaigned them, and that makes this a very special offering," said Hartley. "These five cars will be offered individually and there is no time pressure whatsoever. Our priority, and McLaren’s, is to find the right homes for them." Although no prices were given, they are expected to range from 5 million pounds ($6.7 million) to as much as 10 million. A McLaren MP4-25A raced by Hamilton to victory in Turkey in 2010 sold for 4.8 million pounds in 2021 while a winning 2001 Ferrari raced by Michael Schumacher fetched $7.5 million in New York in 2017.

item.title: Flávio e Lula se enfrentam no primeiro debate; apoiadores ocupam as ruas
item.description: Brasileiros foram às ruas neste domingo em manifestações a favor e contra seus candidatos à Presidência, enquanto o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva e o senador Flávio Bolsonaro se preparavam para seu primeiro debate televisionado, a uma semana do fim da campanha.
item.dc:creator: Brendan O'Boyle, Sebastian Recondio, Luis Nova
item.content:encoded: Brasileiros foram às ruas neste domingo em manifestações a favor e contra seus candidatos à Presidência, enquanto o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva e o senador Flávio Bolsonaro se preparavam para seu primeiro debate televisionado, a uma semana do fim da campanha. Multidões pró-Bolsonaro, vestindo as cores nacionais do Brasil -- amarelo, verde e azul --, lotaram a Avenida Paulista, em São Paulo, onde o candidato discursou para os apoiadores. Apoiadores de Lula, vestidos de vermelho, cor simbólica do Partido dos Trabalhadores, lotaram a praça dos prédios do governo em Brasília, enquanto estudantes que apoiam o presidente protestaram contra Bolsonaro no Rio de Janeiro. As pesquisas mostram uma [USN:S0N45N09L TEXT:"disputa acirrada"] para o segundo turno de 25 de outubro, com Flávio, filho do ex-presidente Jair Bolsonaro, mantendo uma ligeira vantagem após terminar quase 2 pontos percentuais à frente de Lula no [USN:L6N45N1A0 TEXT:"primeiro turno da eleição"], em 4 de outubro. Ambos os candidatos esperam conquistar os 33 milhões de eleitores que ficaram em casa no primeiro turno, o que equivale a cerca de um em cada cinco eleitores qualificados. O debate em São Paulo está marcado para começar às 20h e será transmitido pela emissora Band. O último debate do primeiro turno foi [USN:L1N45M12Z TEXT:"cancelado de última hora"], depois que Lula e Flávio desistiram de participar. Antes um marco da democracia brasileira após o fim da ditadura militar de 21 anos no país, em 1985, os debates presidenciais televisionados perderam relevância à medida que os principais candidatos passaram a optar cada vez mais por não participar. POLÍTICA ACIRRADA Espera-se que o debate entre Flávio Bolsonaro e Lula seja tenso e marcado por ataques pessoais. A polarização entre os apoiadores de Jair Bolsonaro e de Lula domina a política brasileira há quase uma década. Muitos bolsonaristas defendem que Lula deveria estar preso pelos escândalos de corrupção que envolveram o PT, enquanto muitos apoiadores de Lula argumentam que a condenação e a prisão do ex-presidente Bolsonaro por tentativa de golpe de Estado foram justificadas. "Eu não gosto de bandidos. Fora, Lula!", disse a manifestante Vera de Sousa, em São Paulo. No ato em São Paulo, participantes exibiam um grande boneco inflável de Lula vestido com roupa de presidiário. Já em Brasília, manifestantes entoavam gritos de "Bolsonaro na cadeia", enquanto uma imagem do ex-presidente o retratava com as mãos ensanguentadas. "Precisamos que o atual governo continue no poder. Se entrar outro governo, estamos, desculpe a expressão, ferrados", disse a apoiadora de Lula Sonia Maria, durante o ato em Brasília. Lula passou 580 dias preso entre 2018 e 2019 por uma condenação por corrupção que acabou sendo anulada devido a falhas nas investigações e nos procedimentos judiciais. Já o ex-presidente Bolsonaro foi condenado a 27 anos de prisão por conspirar para um golpe de Estado após perder a disputa pela reeleição para Lula em 2022. Ele cumpre a pena em prisão domiciliar por questões de saúde. O filho de Bolsonaro afirmou que o julgamento do pai foi uma "farsa" e prometeu buscar anistia para ele caso seja eleito presidente. "Faltam sete dias para livrarmos o Brasil do PT. E vocês verão Jair Messias Bolsonaro colocando a faixa de presidente no filho dele", disse Flávio à multidão em São Paulo. Em uma postagem na rede social X, Lula afirmou que quem votasse em seu oponente levaria, de "brinde", o pai e os irmãos dele. REVOLTA CONTRA META Uma polêmica sobre se as plataformas da Meta, que incluem o Facebook e o Instagram, trataram os dois candidatos de forma igualitária trouxe nova tensão aos últimos dias da campanha. A coalizão de Lula afirmou que sua conta no Instagram e suas publicações foram restringidas, e o jornal local Folha de S.Paulo divulgou mensagens internas de funcionários da Meta que admitiam [USN:S0N40000V TEXT:"essas restrições"] e afirmavam que a plataforma havia recomendado o perfil de Flávio e seu canal no WhatsApp aos usuários. A Meta afirmou ter enfrentado problemas técnicos globais, mas negou qualquer viés político. “Qualquer sugestão de que a Meta favoreça um lado é falsa”, disse a empresa. Organizações da sociedade civil planejavam realizar um protesto na segunda-feira em frente à sede da Meta em São Paulo contra a "interferência da empresa no processo eleitoral brasileiro", disseram os organizadores em comunicado. (Reportagem de Brendan O'Boyle e Luis Nova em Brasília, com reportagem adicional de Letícia Fucuchima e Sebastian Rocandio em São Paulo)
